name: Urban & Regional Planning
summary: Urban and Regional Planning prepares students to shape how cities, towns, and regions grow and change. Planners work on land use, housing, transportation, and the environment.
description: Urban and Regional Planning majors study planning history and theory, land-use planning and zoning, urban design, transportation planning, housing and community development, environmental planning, economic development, planning law, and public participation. They learn GIS, data analysis, and plan-making skills, often through studio projects for real communities. Internships with city and regional planning departments are common. Many planners later earn a master's degree and the AICP certification. Graduates work for local and regional governments, consulting firms, developers, and nonprofits.
